function: Sensor-aided prediction of channel beamspace (path AoDs) from camera, LiDAR and UE coordinates for BS beam training; non-learned multi-user analog precoder selection follows (pp. 1-2, 8).
system: Downlink MU-MISO OFDM, BS hybrid planar array (16x8 elements, 2 RF chains for U=2, larger for U=4-8), single omnidirectional-antenna UEs, 60 GHz; no RIS (pp. 3, 10).
method: Supervised multimodal DNN (unimodal feature extractors plus fusion network), multi-label AoD identification, trained with BCE plus proposed supervised soft-contrastive loss (SSCL) (pp. 6-8, 10).
data_channel: Raymobtime synthetic ray-tracing dataset, Rosslyn 3D scenario at 60 GHz with LiDAR, camera, coordinates, ten receivers; s008 for training, s009 for testing (p. 10).
test_conditions: Train on s008, test on s009 (same Rosslyn scenario, 60 GHz); U = 2, 4, 6, 8 users, array and beamspace grid set per U (p. 10).
baselines: Full-CSI digital MU-MIMO; 'beam prediction': optimal DFT-codebook beam per UE, the error-free best case of sensor-aided method [31] extended to MU; ground-truth beamspace variant (p. 10).
metrics: Sum spectral efficiency (median, 25th-75th percentile, CDF), mean angular distance and MAE in cosines of predicted AoDs, SSB overhead (pp. 8, 10-13).
complexity: Fusion network 33.502M FLOPs versus 42.947M for the benchmark network of [31]; Algorithm 1 complexity O(U G_theta G_phi + U^3) (p. 13).
openness: none; the authors release no code or data, but the public Raymobtime dataset [27] is used (pp. 1, 10).
q1_support: p. 10: "we use the Raymobtime dataset [27]. This dataset comprises a collection of synthetic ray tracing datasets designed for simulating wireless channels"
q2_support: p. 10: "we use datasets s008 for training our fusion model, while s009 is used for validating the obtained results"; both are "in a synthetic 3D scenario of the city Rosslyn, Virginia"; no new site, band, array or adaptation is tested, and p. 13: "the adoption of generalizable DNN training alongside site-specific model tuning methodologies needs to be considered"
q3_support: p. 10: "Full CSI at the BS: In this scenario, the BS designs FBB assuming noise-less channel estimate"; p. 10: "The BS uses the optimal beam for each UE individually from a DFT codebook" for "[31] when extended to MU setting without prediction error"
q4_support: p. 13: "our proposed fusion network requires 33.502M FLOPs, which is marginally lower than the 42.947M FLOPs needed by the benchmark network"
q5_support: p. 10: "we use the Raymobtime dataset [27]"; p. 1: "publicly available datasets like Raymobtime [27]"
notes: Area 3: the DNN predicts the channel beamspace from camera, LiDAR and coordinates to configure analog beams, and the main metric is the MU sum-SE, so beamforming (area 3) rather than channel estimation (area 2). The MU beamforming algorithm and RZF are not learned (pp. 8-9). q1: Raymobtime is a public ray-tracing dataset, not DeepMIMO or 3GPP; reviewer to confirm. q2 not met: s009 is a separate dataset but from the same Rosslyn scenario and 60 GHz band, and generalization is left as future work (p. 13); if the reviewer counts a separate dataset as new conditions, q2 would be 1. q3: the learned baseline is the error-free best case of sensor-aided beam prediction [31], not a trained network, and the network of [31] is compared only in FLOPs (p. 13); reviewer to confirm. q5 rests on the public Raymobtime dataset; no code is released.
